caption:
Google Business Profile ordering controls: a 4-step check for Black-owned businesses that sell food, now that you can switch off delivery apps yourself.

On October 28, 2026, Google said restaurants can turn off individual third-party ordering providers, like Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub and Instacart, right from the Business Profile dashboard. Each provider gets separate switches for pickup and delivery. Before this, you had to ask every app to remove its link, and Google's help page gave them up to five business days. Google's policy page also says every partner integration starts switched on by default.

Lisa Landsman, who leads SMB success at Google, put it plainly: if a provider no longer fits your operations or your margins, you can turn it off yourself.

Your 4-step check:
1. Open Food ordering in your Business Profile and look at which apps are listed.
2. Go app by app and decide on pickup, delivery, both or neither based on your margins.
3. Add your own ordering link so Google has somewhere direct to send hungry customers.
4. Tap every link that's left and make sure it opens an accurate menu.

Switching an app off only pays when the place you send people instead looks good and works on a phone.
